transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-04 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Alex Rivera (Peregrine Procurement), Dr. Sunita Rao (Peregrine Security), Carlos Mejia (Peregrine ML), Janelle Brooks (Peregrine Legal)

Auto-generated summary: (may contain errors) initial kickoff, procurement interested, need MSA DPA clarif, pilot requested

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with liam our solutions eng, priya from success. quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Alex Rivera: Alex here, sunita, carlos and janelle are on. thanks for organizing.
[00:00:18] Dr. Sunita Rao: hi all.
[00:00:22] Liam O'Rourke: morning, thanks. i have the technical deck up, will jump into sla and private deployment notes shortly.
[00:00:35] Maya Chen: high level goals for the call — get Peregrine's procurement and legal questions scoped, align on MSA/DPA asks, and see if we can scope a short pilot and benchmarks.
[00:00:48] Janelle Brooks: perfect, we'll be focused on data residency, encryption, kms, and indemnity language.
[00:00:53] Carlos Mejia: from infra i'm mostly concerned about network egress, ability to private deploy in our VPC, and whether we can have customer-managed keys.
[00:01:05] Maya Chen: totally. quick note — our platform supports hosted and dedicated and private deployment options. we have customer-managed KMS via HSM integrations for Private.
[00:01:18] Alex Rivera: when you say private deployment, do you mean your control plane still touches anything? what's the telemetry?
[00:01:26] Liam O'Rourke: good question. for Redwood Private the control plane is optional. there's a private control plane package that customers can host; metadata and usage reporting can be configured to not leave the VPC. some telemetry is opt-in, and audit logs are retained in your account.
[00:01:45] Dr. Sunita Rao: that's encouraging. our legal team will want SOC 2 evidence, iso documents, and specifics on whether any PII might be persisted in logs.
[00:01:56] Maya Chen: yes, we will share the security pack — soc2 report, iso, pen test summaries. logs can be configured — we offer token-level redaction and KV cache isolation. note: auto-logging may capture metadata but content retention is configurable per DPA.
[00:02:18] Janelle Brooks: on the MSA specifics — Peregrine needs a clause specifying data residency in eu-west for certain datasets. can we do per-tenant residency?
[00:02:29] Liam O'Rourke: we can pin workloads to region and route by policy — so yes, per-tenant residency is supported for Dedicated and Private. hosted api has region controls but not strict per-tenant residency unless on dedicated.
[00:02:45] Alex Rivera: pricing question — what would a pilot cost? is there a committed minimum for Dedicated or reserved pools?
[00:02:53] Maya Chen: pilots are usually done on hosted credits but for accurate SLA testing we recommend Dedicated trial pools for a short window; committed minimums exist for production Dedicated, but we can arrange a short evaluation commitment or a paid pilot. liam can outline a cost estimate.
[00:03:10] Liam O'Rourke: for the benchmark proposal i'll put together a test harness — typical is 48 hours with representative prompts, seq lengths and concurrency targets. we'll measure p50/p95 latency, token cost and error rate. target is to demonstrate <100ms p50 for the short prompts and stable throughput for long form.
[00:03:34] Carlos Mejia: small flag — our request volumes are spiky during release windows, we need autoscaling burst and a clear plan for fallback to cheaper model variant if capacity is constrained.
[00:03:47] Liam O'Rourke: yes we have routing policies and automatic fallback to model variants; can also configure canary and ramp percent for rollouts.
[00:03:58] Janelle Brooks: indemnity and liability caps — our counsel asked about higher caps for regulated workloads. is that negotiable?
[00:04:06] Maya Chen: that typically goes into enterprise discussions — subject to legal review and procurement thresholds. we'll flag that and include suggested language in the redline.
[00:04:15] Alex Rivera: what about KMS — do you support customer-managed keys and HSM attestation? we need BYOK and key rotation policies documented.
[00:04:24] Liam O'Rourke: we support BYOK for Private and for Dedicated with vault integrations, HSM-backed key wraps. there is an audit trail and rotation APIs. we'll include implementation notes in the security pack.
[00:04:40] Dr. Sunita Rao: micro question — do you ever cache user prompt data in a shared KV? we cannot risk cross-tenant leakage.
[00:04:48] Liam O'Rourke: KV cache is tenant-isolated in dedicated/private; hosted uses prefix isolation but we can enable strict cache isolation or disable shared caching for sensitive customers.
[00:05:05] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[00:05:10] Maya Chen: okay moving to SLAs — we have standard tiers: 99.5, 99.9, 99.95 depending on deployment and entitlements. Dedicated can get 99.9 with committed capacity and some elevated support SLA.
[00:05:26] Janelle Brooks: can you map those to credits/refund bands? we need RTO/RPO, incident response times and credit calculations for partial degradation.
[00:05:36] Priya Patel: for Dedicated we provide credits tied to downtime windows; we have playbooks for incident response and a 1-hour P1 acknowledgement goal with 4-hour mitigation SLO for critical incidents on enterprise packages.
[00:05:52] Alex Rivera: sounds ok. procurement would like the exact language so they can slot it into our template.
[00:05:58] Maya Chen: we'll include a proposed SLA exhibit with the exact credit table and incident timelines in the MSA redline.
[00:06:05] Carlos Mejia: about billing and egress — if we run in our VPC is there an egress fee from Redwood side? we want to avoid double-charging.
[00:06:14] Liam O'Rourke: typically egress within same cloud region is accounted differently; for private deployments hosting inside your VPC you only pay the Redwood license/fees and not network egress; for hosted there are outbound traffic fees on top of token pricing in certain cases. we'll document the billing model in the SOW.
[00:06:36] Janelle Brooks: escrow and termination — can you do source code escrow or model weights escrow? regulator may insist on continuity of operations.
[00:06:46] Maya Chen: for enterprise we do escrow options; model weights are typically third-party — we'll propose an escrow arrangement or a continuity-of-service clause.
[00:06:57] Alex Rivera: timeline — procurement needs to know if we can get through legal review within 3 weeks; is that reasonable?
[00:07:05] Janelle Brooks: if we get redlines within 48 hours from you, we can triage internally in 2 weeks, maybe push for full signoff in 3.
[00:07:14] Maya Chen: so next steps: i will send redlined MSA/DPA and security pack by EOD 8/6, liam will share benchmark plan by 8/8 and we can schedule the pilot for the week of 8/11.
[00:07:25] Dr. Sunita Rao: ai explainability evals — any evals you run on models, can we include a set of our prompts to check hallucination rates?
[00:07:33] Liam O'Rourke: absolutely, include your prompt set, we'll run quality monitoring and produce a regression report. we also have automatic quality alerts tied to evals.
[00:07:44] Alex Rivera: ok good. procurement also asked about vendor risk — do you have cyber insurance limits we can reference?
[00:07:51] Maya Chen: yes cyber liability insurance details are in the security pack. we carry third-party cyber liability and E&O coverage; exact limits will be listed.
[00:07:59] Priya Patel: note for onboarding support — we'll include a 4-week runbook and a dedicated onboarding engineer for the pilot window if you opt in.
[00:08:07] Carlos Mejia: for the pilot please include a cold-start test for long-context generation — we want to measure memory usage and KV persistence.
[00:08:15] Liam O'Rourke: we'll add that to the test cases.
[00:08:20] Speaker 2 (murmur): yep
[00:08:25] Janelle Brooks: summary from legal side — we need per-tenant residency, BYOK, truncated liability carveout discussion, escrow options, and the DPA to permit a 30-day window for data deletion on request.
[00:08:38] Maya Chen: confirmed. we'll scope those items and propose language.
[00:08:44] Alex Rivera: procurement will also ask for a cost projection for a year at expected volumes — can you provide a run-rate once the pilot shows numbers?
[00:08:52] Maya Chen: yes, after the benchmark we can produce an expected cost model with batching and quantization recommendations to optimize unit cost.
[00:09:02] Dr. Sunita Rao: one last technical note — we require SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning for access.
[00:09:08] Liam O'Rourke: supported out of the box for Enterprise; we'll include setup docs.
[00:09:14] Maya Chen: ok, i want to make sure we captured next steps. (recap) maya sends docs by 8/6, liam benchmark by 8/8, pilot 8/11 window, procurement confirms approvers by 8/7. any other items?
[00:09:30] Alex Rivera: that's it from procurement.
[00:09:33] Janelle Brooks: we'll ask for the redlines and escalate any high risk items to our CISO if needed.
[00:09:39] Maya Chen: great, we'll follow-up with calendar invites for the pilot and a draft SLA exhibit. thanks everyone.
[00:09:47] Meeting end: around 15:58 PT
